Considering the issue raised in the present writ petition, learned
counsel for the petitioner is directed to implead the "The Project Director, National Highways
Authority of India, Sahebganj" as respondent no. 6 in the present writ petition.
2. Let necessary insertion in the cause title of the present writ petition be made by learned counsel for the petitioner in course of the day.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner undertakes to serve two copies of the present writ petition to Mrs. Sweety Topno, learned counsel for the respondent no. 6.

4. The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction upon the concerned respondents to pay the balance amount of compensation to the petitioner for acquisition of his land appertaining to Jamabandi No. 42, Survey Plot No. 178, measuring an area of 0.2386 acre, 0.2328 acre & 0.26120 acre of Mouza-Fatehpur, Thana No. 30, Thana-Taljhari, District-Sahebganj for widening and realignment of NH-80 (KM 197 to KM 260).

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the aforesaid land is recorded in the name of Sobel Murmu @ Sopal Murmu and Bobe Murmu both sons of Bada Murmu and Sabdu Murmu.

Thereafter, Sobel Murmu @ Sopal Murmu and Sabdu Murmu died issueless and after their death,
the said land came in exclusive possession of Bobe Murmu.
Bobe Murmu died leaving behind his only son Bhairow Murmu.
Thereafter, Bhairow Murmu also died leaving behind his only son Natwa Murmu.
The petitioner is the only son of Natwa Murmu and great grandson of Bobe Murmu (since deceased).

In the process of acquisition of the said land, Land Acquisition Case No. 50/2016-17 was initiated and notices under Section 3-H of the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act, 1956') [wrongly mentioned as Section 37(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 in the said notice - Annexure-1 series to the writ petition] were issued to the petitioner by the respondent no. 4 - the District Land Acquisition Officer, Sahebganj-cum-Competent Authority under the Act, 1956 fixing total compensation amount of Rs.24,32,887.98/-.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The grievance of the petitioner is that out of the said total compensation amount, only Rs.9,52,478/- has been paid to him, however, the balance amount of Rs.14,80,409.98/- has not been paid despite several representations made to the authorities in this regard.
Under the said compelling circumstance, the petitioner has preferred the present writ petition.

6. Mr. Rahul Saboo, learned GP-II appearing on behalf of the respondent Nos. 1 to 5 and Mrs.
Sweety Topno, learned counsel for the respondent No. 6, jointly submit that the aforesaid contention of the petitioner is required to be factually examined by the respondent No. 4 and hence,
if he prefers a fresh application before the said respondent in this regard, an appropriate decision will be taken within a time frame.
7.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view the nature of the prayer made in the present writ petition, without entering into the merit of the petitioner's aforesaid contention, he is given liberty to prefer a fresh application before the respondent No. 4 in this regard.

On receipt of the said application, the respondent No. 4, after verifying the relevant records and on providing an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner/his representative, shall take an appropriate informed decision within one month from the date of filing of the said application.
8. The present writ petition is accordingly disposed of with aforesaid liberty and direction.
